indicators.name: 10Y-3M Treasury spread
indicators.logic: Yellow below +0.50pp (flattening); red when inverted (<0). Also flag re-steepening within 18 months of an inversion: recessions have often begun after the curve un-inverts, not during the inversion.
indicators.why: Compares the policy rate with the long rate. When short rates exceed long rates, bank lending margins compress and the market is pricing future cuts.

history.2008: Inverted through most of 2006-07; NBER dates the recession start to Dec 2007.
history.2020: Brief inversion in 2019; the Feb 2020 recession was triggered by the pandemic, so the curve gave early but not causal warning.
history.2022: Inverted from late 2022. Lead times have ranged from roughly 6 to 24 months, and the long 2022-24 inversion shows signals can be early or fail.

indicators.track: Daily. Watch level, 3-month change (velocity) and the first close back above zero.

indicators.name: 10Y-2Y Treasury spread
indicators.logic: Same logic as 10Y-3M. 2Y moves on expected Fed policy, so this one reacts earlier to policy-path repricing.
indicators.why: The 2Y yield is the market's average expected policy rate over two years; inversion means cuts are priced in.

history.2022: Inverted from July 2022, reaching roughly -100bp in March 2023 during the regional bank stress.

indicators.name: Fed net liquidity, 6M change
indicators.logic: Net liquidity = Fed balance sheet (WALCL) minus reverse repo (RRP) minus Treasury General Account (TGA), in $bn. Score on the 6-month % change; falling liquidity is a headwind for risk assets.
indicators.why: Reserves are what banks and dealers use to fund balance sheets. RRP and TGA absorb reserves, so the headline balance sheet alone misleads.

history.2008: Large balance-sheet expansion (QE1) began in late 2008, close to the equity low in March 2009.
history.2020: Balance sheet roughly rose from about $4T to about $7T in a few months.
history.2022: QT began June 2022; RRP and TGA swings made net liquidity move differently from the headline balance sheet.

indicators.track: Weekly (Thursday release). Thresholds are heuristic, tune from backtests.

indicators.name: US M2 growth, YoY
indicators.logic: Yellow below 4% growth, red at or below 0% (contraction). Extreme expansion (>15%) is an inflation-risk note, not scored.
indicators.why: Broad money growth feeds spending and asset demand with lags. Global M2 is not freely available as a clean series; this is the US component only.

history.2008: Growth was moderate heading into the crisis.
history.2020: M2 growth exceeded 20% YoY in 2020-21, followed by the 2022 inflation surge.
history.2022: M2 contracted YoY in 2022-23, a sustained contraction not seen in decades.

indicators.track: Monthly. Roadmap: add euro area, China, Japan aggregates (ECB, PBoC, BoJ) for a global M2.

indicators.name: High-yield OAS
indicators.logic: Option-adjusted spread of ICE BofA US High Yield. Yellow above 4.5%, red above 6.5%. Rate of widening matters as much as level.
indicators.why: Prices the default and liquidity risk of the weakest corporate borrowers; widening usually precedes or accompanies equity drawdowns.

history.2008: Spread went above 20% at the peak.
history.2020: Spiked to roughly 11% in March 2020 and retraced quickly after Fed backstops.
history.2022: Reached roughly 6% during the 2022 bear market.

sources: FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE data; FRED currently serves only about 3 years of history)
indicators.track: Daily. Use 3M change as a velocity trigger.

indicators.name: Investment-grade OAS
indicators.logic: Yellow above 1.6%, red above 2.5%. Compare with HY: IG widening confirms stress is spreading beyond weak borrowers.
indicators.why: IG stress means even high-quality issuers face higher funding costs, which hits buybacks, capex and bank balance sheets.

indicators.name: St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index
indicators.logic: Zero is average stress. Yellow above 0, red above 1.5. A composite of rates, spreads and volatility, so it overlaps with other indicators by design.
indicators.why: Serves as a free composite stand-in where bank CDS spreads (proprietary) are unavailable.

history.2022: Elevated but modest; blips in March 2023.

indicators.name: Regional banks drawdown (KRE)
indicators.logic: Percent below the trailing 12-month high of the KRE regional bank ETF. A free proxy for bank-specific stress (CDS data is not freely available).
indicators.why: Regional banks carry the most rate-sensitive balance sheets and deposit-run risk.

history.2020: Sold off hard in March 2020, recovered after backstops.
history.2022: Held up in 2022, then dropped by roughly a third within weeks in March 2023 (SVB, Signature).

indicators.track: Daily; pair with the 2Y yield to see unrealised-loss pressure.

indicators.name: US dollar momentum, 6M
indicators.logic: 6-month % change of the dollar index. A rapid rise tightens global dollar funding and pressures emerging markets and US multinationals.
indicators.why: Most global debt and trade is dollar-denominated; a rising dollar is a global financial-conditions tightener.

history.2008: Dollar surged in the late-2008 flight to safety.
history.2020: Spiked in March 2020 dollar shortage, then reversed on swap lines.
history.2022: DXY peaked near 114 in Sept 2022 amid aggressive Fed hikes.

indicators.name: Copper/Gold ratio, 6M change
indicators.logic: Copper (growth-sensitive) divided by gold (safe haven). A sharp fall signals a global growth scare or flight to safety.
indicators.why: Industrial demand versus safe-haven demand. It tends to track the 10Y yield, so confirm with rates.

history.2008: Fell sharply as global growth collapsed.
history.2020: Dropped in Feb-Mar 2020, rebounded quickly with stimulus.
history.2022: Weakened with growth fears and a strong dollar.

indicators.name: WTI oil, 3M move (absolute)
indicators.logic: Scores the absolute 3-month % change. Large rises are supply or inflation shocks; large falls usually signal demand collapse or a price war.
indicators.why: Oil feeds directly into headline inflation and consumer budgets, and into energy-sector credit.

history.2008: WTI peaked near $145 in July 2008, then collapsed.
history.2020: Futures briefly turned negative on 20 Apr 2020.
history.2022: Spiked to roughly $124 in March 2022 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

indicators.name: 10Y breakeven inflation (de-anchoring)
indicators.logic: Scores distance from a 2.25% anchor: both de-anchoring upward (inflation scare) and collapse (deflation scare) are warnings. Yellow beyond 0.5pp away, red beyond 0.9pp.
indicators.why: Market-implied inflation over 10 years; shows whether policy credibility is intact.

indicators.name: VIX
indicators.logic: Yellow above 22, red above 30. Very low readings (<13) indicate complacency and are noted but not scored.
indicators.why: Implied S&P 500 volatility: demand for equity-index protection.

indicators.name: MOVE (bond volatility)
indicators.logic: Yellow above 110, red above 140. Bond volatility drives collateral values and funding stress, so it often leads equity volatility.
indicators.why: Treasuries are the collateral base of the financial system; instability there forces deleveraging.

history.2022: Around 150-160 in late 2022, then roughly 199 in March 2023.

indicators.name: Sahm rule indicator
indicators.logic: 3-month average unemployment minus its lowest value of the prior 12 months. Red at 0.5pp or more.
indicators.why: A real-time labor-market recession trigger: unemployment tends to accelerate once it starts rising.

history.2008: Triggered close to the start of the Dec 2007 recession.
history.2022: Not triggered in 2022; it triggered in Aug 2024 and was debated as a possible false signal because labor supply was growing.

indicators.name: CBOE SKEW (experimental)
indicators.logic: Elevated SKEW means richer demand for out-of-the-money puts. A poor timing tool on its own; half-weighted.
indicators.why: Measures perceived tail risk in the S&P 500 option market.

indicators.name: Dealer gamma exposure, GEX (experimental)
indicators.logic: Not scored (weight 0) until validated. Negative dealer gamma means hedging flows amplify moves; positive dampens them. Source is a public daily file whose availability is not guaranteed.
indicators.why: Dealer option hedging can amplify intraday and short-horizon moves.
sources: SqueezeMetrics public DIX/GEX file (unofficial, may disappear)
indicators.track: Daily; free dark-pool (DIX) and GEX data are limited, so treat as experimental.
